price_note: aifitlab: motor $40; C615 ESC $60; motor + C615 $100; motor + 420S ESC $80
notes: RoboMaster's 17 mm friction-wheel launcher motor. The listing gives KV both as 2400 and as 875 rpm/V; 21000 rpm at 24 V matches 875. Listing links STEP files and user guides. C615 max 26 V is below a 7S pack's 29.4 V full charge, so it needs a regulated rail. Not a foam-dart part: flywheels and cage would be custom (2.95 mm shaft).
mass_g is per round. 75% heavier than a short dart, so more energy at the same speed; Hasbro sells Rival as 14+ with eyewear recommended. Not recommended for a kids' game.

model: STS3215 / ST3215 12 V 30 kg-cm serial bus servo
price_note: Waveshare SKU 22414, 1 unit (tiers to ~$20.63); RobotShop US $49.22 out of stock

specs.interface: TTL UART half-duplex serial bus, 38400 bps-1 Mbps
specs.encoder: 12-bit magnetic, 4096 counts/turn, 360 deg, no mechanical limit

notes: Stall torque converted from 30 kg-cm at 12 V (7.4 V version: 19.5 kg-cm, 52 rpm). Waveshare lists 89 g; other listings say 55 g. Cheap, light tilt actuator with an absolute encoder, so tilt angle is known at power-up. Needs a 12 V rail (not the 7S bus) and a UART bus adapter. Not PWM controllable.

model: M2006 P36 geared motor (+ C610 ESC)
price_note: aifitlab motor only; C610 ESC V2.0 $250 listed separately
notes: RoboMaster's usual trigger / feed-dial motor (jam detection by watching its speed). Overkill for darts; listed because it is how RoboMaster feeds 17 mm balls. Speeds with C610; Z650 ESC values differ.

vendor: Repeat Robotics (sold by Palm Beach Bots)

specs.firmware: AM32 (reprogrammable with the AM32 config tool)
specs.interface: servo PWM / DShot (AM32); RPM telemetry on this board not confirmed

notes: 6S-capable 5 g ESC, so it runs flywheel motors straight from a regulated 24 V payload rail. Ships with crawler (bi-directional) settings; reflash as uni-directional with RPM telemetry for a closed-loop flywheel. Voltage range is 3-6S LiPo (calc), not a stated rating. Listing shipping weight 15 g.
